question: Of Americans born in 1980, roughly what share earned more at age 30 than their parents had at that age?
answer: About half. Raj Chetty and colleagues found in 2017 that about 90% of Americans born in 1940 out-earned their parents at 30, against about 50% of those born in 1980. Most of the fall came from growth going to the top, not from slower growth. The ladder was still there; fewer rungs reached the middle.
move: Ask who receives growth, not only how fast an economy grows.
ask: Am I measuring my progress against my parents, and is that the fairest comparison?
trap: About 90%, anchored on the post-war pattern of each generation outdoing the last.
reference: Chetty, Grusky, Hell, Hendren, Manduca & Narang, The Fading American Dream: Trends in Absolute Income Mobility Since 1940, Science 356 (6336), 2017
